steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Only candles lighting the corridors. Is the palace cutting back power usage too?

steps.name: Attentive Servant
steps.text: His Imperial Majesty wishes to share the conserved energy with the people.

steps.name: Attentive Servant
steps.text: Rest assured, this is simply a pragmatic measure of frugality. Life in the palace has not been affected, nor has this year's Winter Ball.

steps.name: Attentive Servant
steps.text: Here we are. May I take your coat, Miss Rostova?

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: That's very kind of you.

steps.name: Attentive Servant
steps.text: It is my duty.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: So bright...

steps.name: Attentive Servant
steps.text: I will take my leave, then.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: One moment. I have some questions—

steps.name: Noblewoman
steps.text: —Natashenka?

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Countess Vorontsova?

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Gosudar-batyushka... it's really you, poor girl!
The noblewoman hurriedly approaches Rosa, so excited she can hardly maintain her aristocratic demeanor.
She grabs Rosa's arm tightly, as though confirming she has not seen a ghost.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Natashenka... oh, I'm so glad to see you... alive and well...

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: It broke my heart to hear what happened in Chernobog. Why would fate be so cruel to such a kind family?

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Thank you for your sympathy. We lost some property, but it's nothing compared to the safety of the family... and anyway, it's all in the past.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Yes, yes, let us leave all the painful memories in the past... you have no idea how glad I was to read your letter that you were coming to Deity Grypherburg.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: I wish you could enjoy a peaceful time here, but the capital is hardly a peaceful place these days.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Malcontents and ingrates everywhere—as though the troubles stirred by those insolent military brutes were not enough, now unruly commoners want to turn Deity Grypherburg upside-down.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Oh, look at me, this is no way to talk to the daughter of an old friend that I haven't seen in years. You've only just gotten back, of course you have no idea! I'm afraid I'm always on edge these days, I hardly get any sleep at night.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Not at all. I'm glad you're sharing the news with me.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: You're a good girl, but this is not a good time to talk of such things.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Is your mother well, Natashenka? What about your father, Andrey?

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: If he's in the capital without saying a word, sending you alone to the Winter Ball...

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: I suppose I've been a poor friend, and allowed our families to drift apart.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Countess, that's not it at all. Father asked me to send you his regards if I saw you, and to beg your pardon for falling out of touch.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: And of course, I do not need to tell you that you are Mother's best friend, but the House of Rostov is focusing our full attention on what assets we have left in the Central Governorate.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: 'We must not lose any more prestige,' and I regret to say... they are fully occupied, for the time being.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: I understand, but you should say, 'Therefore, I am here.'

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Look at you, a proper young lady all grown up. You are a perfect representative of the House of Rostov!

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: I must say, you show better manners and dignity than many native Grypherburgers... I'm sure the Rostov name will be known throughout the capital before long.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: No... I still have much to learn.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Speaking of which, I would very much like to ask about the present situation...

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Have patience, young Natashenka. I understand your unease, but this is not something that can be explained in a few words.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Learn to observe with your own eyes. There is no better opportunity than this. What you should do now, is go enjoy the Winter Ball.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Until His Majesty arrives, set aside all the troubling questions, all the answers you eagerly seek, and all the wild theories about what the future holds. Enjoy the present.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Dance, laugh, do as youth ought to.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: And if a young officer catches your eye, I will stake my reputation to be your matchmaker, for the sake of your mother, even if it's stubborn old Bolkonsky's—

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Enjoy the peace of His Majesty's protection. It is a privilege for those of us who live here in the capital, those of us who are loyal.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: You must learn this in order to fully integrate yourself, Natashenka.

a.text: '...You must learn this in order to fully integrate yourself.'

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: ...The miners are still hungry. Even in Grypherburg, the residents of Odoyev Raion can no longer afford heating, while Katorga Raion has seen power and heat cut completely upon work stoppage.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: But for them, the show must go on.

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: I don't understand... didn't that person say His Majesty is reducing the palace's electricity use? What happened to the energy conserved? Why—

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: This is all such nonsense. Dealing with big shots is such a hassle.

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: Is Rosa gonna be okay in there?

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Natalya spoke to us a few days before the Student Assembly general meeting about going into the ball as the scion of House Rostov to gather information.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Certain things are known only to the aristocracy, after all. And more information never hurts, regardless of where it comes from.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Sonya believes she can do it, and I have no reason to object. The contents of these conversations are as expected. Things seem to be going smoothly so far, and the audio feed is clear.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: We have to thank that student they call Botani for this. Her equipment has worked out even better than I hoped.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: All we need to do is to cooperate with the protestors and follow the plan.

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: Zima's waving at us! We should go to her.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: I think she's talked things over with the others. We'll pack up and head over.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Leto, are you staying here or...?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Shh, gimme a sec.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Something's happening.

steps.name: Worried Noble
steps.text: I thought this year's Winter Ball would be cancelled...

steps.name: Worried Noble
steps.text: Those insolent traitors are attempting to coerce His Imperial Majesty by force of arms. But I'm not sure how the tsar intends to deal with them...

steps.name: Proud Noble
steps.text: All the more important that we hold our heads high and continue doing what we must. His Imperial Majesty has both courage and vision.

steps.name: Proud Noble
steps.text: This is the strongest possible response. It proves that there is nothing to be feared from the chaos, that we will not be beaten by traitors who have already failed once.

steps.name: Proud Noble
steps.text: As for those who do not see clearly, and choose to stand with the traitors... we will place flowers on their graves, this time next year.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Look out!
—I'm sorry—

steps.name: Proud Noble
steps.text: You have ruined not only the young lady's dress, but also a cup of fine wine... sudar'.
I'm so sorry! Please forgive the offense, Duchess Volkina—

steps.name: Proud Noble
steps.text: You did not offend me, but you should apologize to the young lady whose dress you have soiled.
Erm, I apologize, baryshnya...

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: It's alright.

steps.name: Worried Noble
steps.text: Who let this buffoon in?

steps.name: Proud Noble
steps.text: He could hardly be a nameless commoner if the servants let him in. What is your name?

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Ah! Please call me Pavlovich, a humble deputy of the Duma. I was recently appointed magistrate by His Imperial Majesty, serving as special representative for recent matters in Katorga Raion—

steps.name: Proud Noble
steps.text: A representative of Katorga Raion? Ah, I remember now.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: You know me? I'm honored!

steps.name: Proud Noble
steps.text: Of course, of course. I heard the State Council was having difficulty finding someone to deal with the Katorga problem. I'm sure you must be a remarkable talent, if the responsibility has fallen upon your shoulders.

steps.name: Proud Noble
steps.text: I would have sent someone to congratulate you, if I was not busy arranging winter supplies for the Second Army.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: You flatter me, Your Grace... I have been serving in Katorga for two months now.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: In fact, I do not know why I was given such an important responsibility, but I certainly would not dream of disappointing His Imperial Majesty.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: As you may know, Katorga Raion is not as worthless as people think. All this old industrial district needs is an opportunity to revitalize itself...

steps.name: Worried Noble
steps.text: (Whisper) Why have I never heard of him?

steps.name: Proud Noble
steps.text: Perhaps you've been spending too much time on your luxurious estate and grown out of touch with the personnel movements of the central government. At least read a few newspapers while you sit on your rocking chair in your garden.

steps.name: Worried Noble
steps.text: All the news does is make one more troubled.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Of course, I am unworthy of Your Serenity's attention, Count Golitsyn—I understand that this has been an exemplary year for your winery, and you must be very busy...

steps.name: Proud Noble
steps.text: Enough flattery. I believe you still owe this young lady a formal apology.

steps.name: Proud Noble
steps.text: What is your name, baryshnya?

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: I am Natalya Rostova, Your Grace.

steps.name: Proud Noble
steps.text: Rostova? I am not familiar with the name...

steps.name: Worried Noble
steps.text: Neither am I.

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Ah! Your father must be Count Andrey Rostov of Chernobog!

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: You know of my father?

steps.name: Pavlovich
steps.text: Of course! His Serenity demonstrated such foresight when he pulled out from Chernobog just in time, narrowly avoiding complete ruin!

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: ...That's all in the past now.

steps.name: Proud Noble
steps.text: I see you are surprisingly... knowledgeable, Gospodin Pavlovich.

steps.name: Proud Noble
steps.text: But you ought to get changed, young lady. Even the best wine was not made to be tasted by silk.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Yes, spasibo...
Rosa hurries away from the embarrassing scene. She can still hear the excited conversation going on behind her as she leaves.

steps.name: Flattering Voice
steps.text: Duchess Volkina! I hear that you oppose the motion to decommission Katorga Raion. I am naturally of the same mind...

steps.name: Flattering Voice
steps.text: ...The factories are still...

steps.name: Flattering Voice
steps.text: ...Perhaps we can work together...

steps.name: Stern Noble
steps.text: ...Watch your words, Melnikov. Not even His Imperial Majesty has made an official statement on the events of the Far North.

steps.name: Arrogant Noble
steps.text: You misunderstand. I am not leveling an accusation towards you or the Grand Duchess.

steps.name: Arrogant Noble
steps.text: However, I have long expressed concerns about Breskenoy, long before Yelizaveta's transgressions in the Far North, yet your camp unanimously swore to His Imperial Majesty that her loyalty should not be questioned.

steps.name: Arrogant Noble
steps.text: You, and every single member of the old guard, have betrayed the trust of the State Council and His Imperial Majesty.

steps.name: Stern Noble
steps.text: Then I look forward to your speech at the hearing. You would do well not to change a single word, that everyone might hear how you slander the foundations of our empire.

steps.name: Arrogant Noble
steps.text: There is no need to wait until then.

steps.name: Arrogant Noble
steps.text: I will expose your crimes to His Imperial Majesty when he attends tonight's ball!
The angry shouting has drawn the attention of the crowd. Several servants hurry to the scene, trying to placate the angry aristocrat.
Rosa pulls on her sleeves to ward off the cold, though the fireplaces in the ballroom burn hotter than anywhere else in Ursus, and the heat is always on.
A servant is replacing the fragrance. The smell of citron and neroli cover up the stinging scent of evaporating alcohol. Rosa lets out a long sigh.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Are you alright, Natashenka? Have you not yet found an appropriate conversation partner?

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Oh dear, what happened to your dress? Did someone insult you? Give me a name, and I will teach them a lesson!

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Please, Countess, there is no need to be angry. It's a mark of honor for assisting a noble lady.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: You have a heart of gold, my child, but please, take care of your own safety first next time. Who knows what those sycophants might do?

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: I appreciate your concern, but that was the most interesting thing to happen to me tonight.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Most of what I've heard has to do with the Grand Duchess. I tried to understand and ask questions, but I lack the necessary knowledge to continue the conversation.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: This is why your parents sent you to Grypherburg, my dear Natashenka.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: I have seen many young ladies give their souls to cooks, tailors, and doctors, but not the great people who write laws, quell rebellions, and set taxes...

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Even if they are always caring about us.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: I understand, but today I'm simply the heir of a humble count with naught but a few small holdings in the Central Governorate. How might I catch a gaze that these busy lords only occasionally cast?

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: ...I should make myself clearer, since you're my old friend's only daughter.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Politics is a part of all our lives. No one is immune, especially not those upon whom a title of nobility has conferred a heavy responsibility.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Are these responsibilities carried out by engaging in small talk in a place like this?

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Natashenka...

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: You misunderstand the reason we talk here. These words are not necessarily announcements of measures certain to be implemented, nor do they necessarily represent our true views.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Then... why?

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: To fit in. To know which people to avoid, and which to befriend.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: One signature may be all it takes to rebuild your parents' fortune, to keep your children out of the trenches, to allow your friends to sleep soundly on a grand estate.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Do not think you can avoid their gazes by indulging in pleasure. It will only cause those gazes to harden, and permit no question.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: That is how a highly effective social scene operates, Natashenka.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: ...Looks like I still have much to learn.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: And time is the one thing that young people have aplenty.

steps.name: Noble A
steps.text: (Whisper) It's the Chairman—

steps.name: Noble B
steps.text: And Vice Chairman Vasily Gorchikov! This is a rare sight. They are hardly ever seen together outside of the State Council...

steps.name: Noble A
steps.text: The Chairman is rarely seen at the balls, but His Imperial Majesty has not yet arrived... is this a sign?

steps.name: Noble B
steps.text: Perhaps they are trying to present a picture of calm.

steps.name: Noble A
steps.text: It may be too late for that.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Those two...?
All eyes are on the two men who just entered. The crowd parts to allow them to proceed to the middle of the hall.
The greetings from the crowd are loud, though their sincerity is uncertain.
Rosa carefully observes the pair from the crowd.
The black-haired man walks through the crowd in silence, not the slightest emotion on his face. His gaze is firm, but clearly fatigued, fixed on the empty space in front of him.
The man whom they call Vice Chairman walks behind the black-haired man who is a head shorter than he is, respectfully keeping a short distance while nodding and smiling in response to the crowd.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: ...The blonde one is Duke Vasily Gorshkov, colonel-in-chief of the Imperial Guard, and executive Vice Chairman of the State Council.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: (Whisper) And the black-haired one in front of him is—

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Chairman Islam Witte.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Yes... everyone in Grypherburg should recognize him.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Actually, I watched the Speech at the Inauguration Ceremony of the Tulskaya Special Technical School on the intercity net. It was an impressive speech, concise and sincere.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Ah, the intercity net... I will never understand such newfangled things.

steps.name: Countess Vorontsova
steps.text: Go before them, Natashenka. Listen to what these people talk about. This is a learning opportunity.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Yes, Countess, I will—
The sharp sound of glass cracking interrupts the cheerful conversations around the hall, as everyone looks around for its source.

steps.name: Noble A
steps.text: Count Osadchy, are you feeling unwell?

steps.name: Noble B
steps.text: ...No, no! It's them! They're downstairs!

steps.name: Noble A
steps.text: What? Who turned off the lights—power outage?

steps.name: Noble B
steps.text: The palace wouldn't lose power just like this! It must be the mob—

steps.name: Noble A
steps.text: Are the duty officers of the palace so incompetent they can't even maintain an electrical switch—

steps.name: Noble B
steps.text: ...Look outside!

steps.name: Noble B
steps.text: There's a mob right outside the window!
